conviction_note: The findings sum to +0.4: the ABS servicer reports show no new credit deterioration, the soft comparison points to a revenue beat, and faster wholesale depreciation offsets part of that. I emit half the sum, +0.2, because this name has sold 6 of its last 8 prints, sold an 8% revenue beat and a 36% EPS beat by 9% in June, and carries +5.27 vol points of put skew. Nothing I found says the option market is wrong about this print.
bar: Consensus Q2 FY27 revenue $6.94bn and EPS $0.71. Two sources agree: investing.com 2026-09-28 (https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/carmax-earnings-in-focus-as-turnaround-strategy-faces-test-93CH-4885803) and Trader Central 2026-09-19 (https://traderc.com/kmx-q2-fy2027-earnings-options/). Zacks has $0.67 / $7.05bn and TradingKey ~$0.72 / ~$6.97bn. Company guide: retail GPU down about $200 YoY for FY27, better than the $300 first assumed (Q1 slides, https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/carmax-q1-fy27-slides-earnings-beat-amid-cost-cuts-caf-growth-93CH-4747511), and $200m of SG&A exit-rate savings by the end of FY27. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue: my estimate is about $7.1-7.2bn.
positioning_check: Short interest 6.7% of free float per ORTEX, data 2026-09-26, down from a 9.4% peak (~13.8m shares) in mid-August. Borrow cost 0.45%. Put/call 0.55 against a 20-day average of 0.50 (https://ortex.news/articles/173488/kmx-options-defensiveness-sharpens-as-shorts-accelerate-their-exit). Days to cover about 4.6: my own arithmetic, ~9.8m shares short over the baseline's 2.15m 20-day average volume. An undated snippet gave 5.0 days. This is not a crowded short, and shorts have covered into the print, so there is little squeeze fuel either way. The baseline skew of +5.27 vol points pays for downside, and the event-implied move is 11.56%.

findings.finding: CarMax's own ABS servicer reports through August 2026 show no new credit deterioration in the securitised Tier 1 book, which the 10-Q puts at 95.6% of the portfolio. The 2025-3 trust at 13 months (31+ day delinquency 1.75%, cumulative net loss 0.49%) tracks 2024-3 at the same age a year earlier (1.63%, 0.60%). The problem 2023 vintage (trust 2023-4) deteriorated April to August 2026 by +1.22pp of delinquency, against +1.11pp over the same months of 2025, and its cumulative net loss accrual slowed. So a repeat of Q2 FY26's $71.3m reserve build for the 2022-2023 vintages looks unlikely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has been the downside line. Q2 FY26 (2025-09-25) fell 20.07% on a $142.2m provision that included the $71.3m vintage build (https://investors.carmax.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2025/CarMax-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results/default.aspx). Q1 FY27 (2026-06-17) fell 8.98% partly on CAF credit worry about Tier 2 expansion, even though the provision fell to $95.6m. The market punishes credit surprises. The absence of one has not been shown to pay.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews cite only the May allowance ratio (2.95%, up from 2.78%) and the Manheim index as the credit tells (traderc 2026-09-19). None cites the June-August trust data. If the market had read these reports, put skew would not still be rising into the print on a name whose last big credit shock was a vintage build. ORTEX has put/call 2.4 standard deviations above its average. The caveat, which the size reflects: consensus EPS up 11.5% YoY already assumes no repeat build, so this removes a tail rather than moving the bar. The Tier 2 book, whose day-one provisions are the live worry, is not in these trusts.
findings.independence: Same document family, different trusts and dates: 2024-3 August 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2029255/000202925525000048/a2024-3ex991091525.htm); 2023-4 August 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995430/000199543026000047/a2023-4ex991091526.htm), April 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995430/000199543026000025/a2023-4ex991051526.htm), August 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995430/000199543025000048/a2023-4ex991091525.htm) and April 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995430/000199543025000025/a2023-4ex991051525.htm); 2024-4 August 2026, 22 months old, 2.04% delinquency and 0.86% cumulative net loss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2037519/000203751926000048/a2024-4ex991091526.htm). All are one servicer's reports, so they count as one finding. Independent support: TransUnion has industry 60+ day delinquency stable near 1.51% in Q2 2026 (snippet via https://www.cbtnews.com/auto-delinquencies-climb-as-lower-income-americans-struggle-with-car-payments/).

findings.finding: The revenue bar of $6.94bn (+5.3% YoY) implies roughly flat retail units against a Q2 FY26 comparison of -6.3% comps. Management blamed that quarter on demand pulled into Q1 by tariffs and on price competitiveness hurt by depreciation. Q1 FY27 ran a two-year comp stack of +7.3% (+8.1% then -0.8%). Cox says used retail sales strengthened through August, with retail days' supply falling from 46 to 44, so units and revenue probably clear the bar by about 3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not paid. Q1 FY27 beat revenue by about 8% ($8.01bn against ~$7.39bn) and EPS by 36%, and the stock fell 8.98% (https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/06/17/carmax-kmx-q1-earnings.html). Only 2 of the last 8 prints rose (+6.59% on 2025-06-20, when Q1 FY26 comps were +8.1%, and +3.45%).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue has been too low two prints running. Q1 needed an 8% beat, and the Q2 bar still implies little unit recovery against the easiest comparison in years. If the comparison were priced, published revenue estimates would sit nearer $7.2bn than $6.94bn. The counterweight is already in the size: this is arithmetic anyone can do from public numbers, the buy-side whisper is probably above $6.94bn, and the June print showed this holder base selling a revenue beat. I sized the reaction at 0.4, not the ~1.0 the fact alone might carry.
findings.independence: Cox Automotive August 2026 index report: used retail sales picking up through August, days' supply 44, down from 46 (https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/manheim-used-vehicle-value-index-august-2026-trends/). The pull-forward explanation for Q2 FY26: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/carmax-inc-kmx-q2-2026-190234681.html. Q1 FY26 comps of +8.1%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1170010/000117001025000080/q1fy26earningsrelease.htm. Management said on 2026-06-17 that it expected the unit momentum to continue (https://equibles.com/stocks/kmx/calls/2027-q1).

findings.finding: Wholesale values fell about 2.2% during the quarter (Manheim index 212.9 in June, ~209.8 in July, 208.2 in August 2026). Cox called the August decline 'more than typical'. On the index's own year-over-year figures, the same window in 2025 fell only about 0.5%. Depreciation within the quarter is the mechanism CarMax itself blamed for lost price competitiveness in Q2 FY26, so it pressures wholesale GPU (Q2 FY26: $993) and possibly retail GPU beyond the ~$200 guided decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GPU compression drove the June 2026 sell-off (-8.98%; retail GPU -$230 to $2,177) and the April 2026 sell-off (-15.12%; GPU -$207 to $2,115, https://investors.carmax.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/CarMax-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results/default.aspx). Q2 FY26's -20.07% came with the depreciation explanation.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The Manheim index is on every preview's watch-list (traderc names it as one of the two numbers that matter), and the finding agrees with the +5.27 put skew and the -7.7% 20-day run-up. What may not be priced is the year-over-year contrast in the depreciation slope, which previews quote only as a level. It is an industry proxy, and whether it reaches this company is a hypothesis this quarter, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Cox August report: 208.2, -0.9% MoM, YoY growth down to 0.4% from +2.1% in June (https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/manheim-used-vehicle-value-index-august-2026-trends/). June value 212.9 (https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/q2-2026-muvvi/). Same publisher throughout, so this is one series.

outside_window.finding: CarMax will hold a Strategic Update in 'late fall 2026', with no date announced, to detail the key initiatives and milestones of the four-pillar plan. Any multi-year targets land then, not in this print's window.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filings by CarMax since 2026-06-20. The only 8-K is item 5.02 (Chief People Officer Diane Cafritz leaving 2026-12-31, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1170010/000117001026000098/kmx-20260729.htm). There is no quiet 8-K and no pre-announcement.

Form 4s. Insiders bought in June after the Q1 drop: CEO Barr 9,400 shares at $53.005 on 2026-06-22 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1170010/000117001026000067/wk-form4_1782336051.xml); director O'Neil 9,600 at $52.36. Nothing since June. Three months old and priced.

Q1 FY27 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1170010/000117001026000055/kmx-20260531.htm): the allowance rise is attributed to Tier 2 expansion and seasonality, and the $500m term loan of 2026-06-15 is refinancing. No new risk factor.

The September 2026 layoff of 145 corporate staff is wire copy, consistent with the $200m SG&A plan, and not a new fact (https://www.pymnts.com/personnel/2026/carmax-cuts-145-corporate-jobs-in-third-layoff-round-in-11-months/).

Carvana's Q2 2026 (197k retail units, +38%, guide for a sequential Q3 increase; https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729523749/en/Carvana-Announces-Record-Second-Quarter-2026-Results) reads across to industry demand and to share loss, and is in the price two months on.
Alternative unit data (web traffic, inventory counts). No citable source found.
Macro: the Fed's 2026-09-16 hike and gas at $4.06 against $3.14 a year ago are in the wire and the sector tape (Carvana -5.7% on 2026-09-28). They are not company-level.
baseline_tension: What I found leans mildly positive: no new credit deterioration and an easy unit comparison. That cuts against the +5.27 put skew, a reaction history of 6 down in 8, and a 20-day run-up of -7.7%. None of it is strong enough to say the option market is wrong, so the emitted number is half the finding sum and close to zero.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): cut the revenue/units finding from +1.0 to +0.4, because this name sold an 8% revenue beat and a 36% EPS beat by 9% in June and has fallen on 6 of its last 8 prints.

Lessons 5 and 7 (a narrow proxy loses; positioning is the thing to beat): cut the Manheim depreciation finding from -1.0 to -0.5. It is an industry proxy whose effect on this company is a hypothesis this quarter, and it agrees with the put skew and the run-up, so it is largely priced.

Lesson 3 (the caveat has to reach the number): emitted expected_move_pct of +0.2, half the +0.4 finding sum, because baseline_tension says the evidence runs against the skew and the reaction history. The pre-lessons draft had +0.3 on a +0.5 sum.

Left standing: the ABS credit finding at +0.5. It rests on primary documents and lands on the credit line this stock trades on. Lesson 9 is handled in the text: the trusts cover Tier 1, 95.6% of the portfolio, and not the growing Tier 2 book.
Lesson 6: the bar is sourced to two agreeing estimate sources plus the company's GPU and SG&A guide, so no cap applies. The strategic update sits in outside_window.
